title: POC weekly sync - acceptance criteria & fallback orchestration
summary: Weekly POC sync to validate acceptance criteria for pilot go decision. Reviewed last week's load run results, KV cache hit tuning, canary traffic steering plan, and fallback orchestration. Agreed action items: reproduce spike test with 1.5x traffic, finalize rollback runbook, Redwood to provide updated playbook and pricing delta for dedicated fallback tier.
action_items: Priya: Validate alert thresholds in PagerDuty and share runbook snippet by 2027-09-14
Liam (Redwood SE): Run 1.5x spike test with KV cache disabled/enabled and upload CSV by 2027-09-13
Maya (AE): Send pricing delta for Dedicated failover lane and updated SLA language by 2027-09-12
Tom (Nimbus Security): Share SOC2 scope questions and KMS key management preferences by 2027-09-15
next_steps: Redwood to update cutover and rollback runbook and share link to doc
Customer to run internal smoke test and confirm SLO gating window next Tuesday
Schedule final go/no-go on 2027-09-20 cadence meeting
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-10 16:00 PDT — Duration 58m. Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Priya (Lead SRE - Nimbus), Carlos (CTO), Anika (Data Platform), Tom (Security).

Summary (auto): go/no-go criteria alignment, observability gating and fallback orchestration.

[00:00] Maya: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna run through the acceptance criteria and the fallback orchestration plan for the pilot, quick check — still good with 58 minutes?
[00:07] Priya: yup good here, we have Carlos on the line too.
[00:12] Carlos: hi all, hope we can get through the runbook bits — we had one surprise in the last spike run.
[00:17] Liam: quick agenda — results recap, KV cache tuning notes, canary/A-B steering, fallback playbook and telemetry gating, security Qs.
[00:26] Anika: sounds good.

[03:05] Liam: ok results first — last Thursday we ran the 300k token burst over 30 minutes. p50 latencies were about 190ms, p95 spiked roughly to 1.4s on the hosted lane with default batching, CPU/GPU utilization looked fine but we saw a KV cache hit-rate drop from 82% down to ~48% under that pattern.
[03:30] Priya: yeah that drop is what bit us — some of the prefixes were not colliding the way we expected, so a lot more cold loads. That explains the p95 tail.
[03:45] Maya: important callout — we saw cost-per-token increase ~22% during the spike because of those cold KV loads and less efficient batching.
[04:02] Carlos: so is that a config issue we can tune or something inherent to our traffic shape?
[04:10] Liam: mostly config and prompt engineering; two levers: (1) adjust prefix hashing thresholds so similar prompts get cached more aggressively, (2) increase max-batch-window slightly to improve batching during bursts. Both have latency vs cost tradeoffs.
[04:26] Priya: we need exact numbers — what does increasing batch window by 20ms do to p95?
[04:33] Liam: from our microbench, +20ms batch window drops cost ~8% and p95 improves by ~150ms in steady state, but in worst-case spikes it can add noise. We'll attach the microbench csv.

[06:12] Jordan: also we tested the dedicated fallback lane — when we fail over to Dedicated the p95 dropped to 900ms but cost increased ~40%. Maya, you said there was a dedicated failover pricing delta?
[06:22] Maya: yes, for a reserved-failover configuration we quoted an incremental commit that buys the warm pool capacity; i'll send the exact numbers after the call. It's intended as a safety lane for our SLOs.

[08:40] Anika: about the canary plan — we're thinking A-B style where 10% goes to the new model variant for 2 hours then 25% then 50%. Do you have auto-revert on SLO exceed?
[08:52] Liam: yes, Redwood runbooks support SLO-gated rollbacks. You can set multiple metrics: p95 latency, error-rate, and quality regressions (we'll discuss eval hooks). If any gate trips we route 100% back to baseline and flag on-call.
[09:10] Priya: what are the SLO thresholds recommended for us? Our internal SLO is 95% requests < 800ms.
[09:18] Liam: for your traffic profile we recommend gating at p95 > 1.1s for 5m and error-rate > 0.5% sustained over 2m. That gives a short window to trigger fallback before users notice severe degradation.

[11:01] Carlos: the last outage had cascade effects in downstream eventing; we need clear circuit-breaker and throttling steps in the runbook.
[11:10] Jordan: agreed — we'll include traffic shaping rules (rate limiter fallback), request queuing thresholds, and a manual abort button in the console.

[13:30] Tom: security question — when we fail to Dedicated or Private, keys and logs — do those stay within our KMS and audit logs? We can't have plaintext tokens leaving our VPC.
[13:45] Maya: for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS and logs remain in your syslog/S3 depending on config. For Hosted+Dedicated we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (if you pick that option). We'll map options in writing.
[14:05] Tom: also SOC 2 scope — we needed confirmation that the PII handling during inference is in scope and that you retain audit logs for 90 days minimum.
[14:15] Maya: we are SOC 2 compliant; retention options are configurable — i'll include our SOC 2 cert and the audit log retention table.

[16:00] Liam: back to telemetry — we recommend these signals for canary gating: p50/p95, model error-rate, KV cache hit-rate, batch sizes, and inference QPS. Also add a quality eval subset sampled at 1% to capture hallucination/regression signals.
[16:18] Anika: sampling 1% seems ok, where will those evals run?
[16:24] Liam: either in Redwood Optimize evals pipeline or you can host local evals and push metrics to our hooks; both supported.

[18:40] Priya: runbook details — we need step-by-step: pre-checks (k8s node readiness, memory, KV cache warm), smoke tests (5 test prompts), gating windows, rollback, postmortem owner. Can you provide a template?
[18:58] Jordan: yes we have a runbook template; i'll attach a version tuned for your infra. It'll include explicit curl checks, synthetic prompt list, and sample Grafana dashboards.

[21:25] Carlos: curious about graceful degradation — if model latency climbs, can we degrade to a smaller quantized variant automatically?
[21:32] Liam: yes, Redwood runtime supports model variants and auto-fallback policies. You can set routing policy: prefer low-cost variant if p95 > threshold or if queue length > threshold. The tradeoff is potential quality drop; we'll tie that to eval-based regression alerts.

[24:05] Priya: about KV cache — you mentioned prefix hashing thresholds; can we tweak that without redeploy?
[24:13] Liam: yes most KV parameters are runtime flags; you can change them via the config API and they take effect without restarting, though warm-up time matters. We recommend a small ramp.

[26:40] Maya: let's discuss spike reproduction — Liam, you'll run 1.5x the traffic pattern with KV cache toggled, and upload raw CSVs. Priya will validate alerts.
[26:51] Priya: yes i'll check alert noise and adjust PD escalation.
[27:00] Tom: i want to verify that when failover happens we don't create duplicate events to downstream queues; is there an idempotency hook?
[27:09] Liam: we provide idempotency tokens at request-level and an event dedupe guide for downstreams; we'll include patterns.

[30:00] Maya: runbook dry-run — who will be on-call during the cutover? Carlos?
[30:07] Carlos: I can be on call for the first hour; Priya will own the ops handoff.
[30:12] Priya: yep i'll be primary.

[33:30] Anika: monitoring — can we get token level cost breakouts per route and model variant? We need that for product analytics.
[33:40] Jordan: yes console shows token-level cost by route and model; we can also export to your billing bucket hourly.

[36:20] Maya: decision timeline — we suggested final internal smoke by 2027-09-17 and go/no-go meeting 2027-09-20. Is that still feasible?
[36:30] Carlos: yes assuming the spike tests pass and runbook looks solid.

[39:45] Priya: one last thing — error handling for downstream latency, we want a canary that de-rates traffic to 5% if DB latency > 200ms. Can that be part of the routing policy?
[39:56] Liam: yes, define a custom metric in Redwood routing rules; when DB latency metric exceeds threshold we route to a less loady path. Will include example rule.

[42:00] Tom: security follow up — i'll send our KMS key names and the compliance checklist, can you map what's supported?
[42:08] Maya: absolutely, Tom send the list and we'll map it.

[45:10] Jordan: quick recap of action items and owners (see action_items). Any blockers?
[45:18] Priya: none right now besides needing the runbook template and the spike CSV.
[45:25] Carlos: also need pricing for the Dedicated failover lane.
[45:28] Maya: i'll send pricing delta and SLA.

[47:00] Anika: small note about test data — we will obfuscate PHI but keep semantics; hope that's OK for eval hooks.
[47:08] Liam: totally fine, we'll accept obfuscated data for quality checks.

[50:00] Maya: final notes: we'll update the runbook and pricing, Liam will run the spike test and share artifacts, Priya will validate alerts and smoke tests, Tom shares KMS mapping. Next meeting scheduled 2027-09-20 09:00 PDT for go/no-go.
[50:20] Carlos: great, thanks everyone.
[50:25] Priya: thanks.
[50:27] Maya: thanks all, end call.

Auto-generated Questions: ["What are the exact SLO thresholds for gating?", "Can we get a step-by-step rollback runbook?", "How will keys be managed during failover?"]

Attachments referenced: [runbook-template-v2.md (shared), spike-results-2027-09-09.csv (to be uploaded), SOC2-certificate.pdf (link to Redwood docs), pricing-failover-delta.xlsx (to be sent by AE)].
